/> In it last summer. <break time="0.8s" /> Sprowls and Mooney, a vaudeville act. <break time="0.8s" /> Kept it for three months. <break time="0.8s" /> And Miss B aretta Sprowls. <break time="0.8s" /> Had her marriage certificate framed. <break time="0.8s" /> And hung over the dresser. <break time="0.8s" /> Theater people mostly come here, sir. <break time="0.8s" /> Because this is the theatrical district. <break time="0.8s" /> And actor people never stay long anywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> She added. <break time="0.8s" /> And he paid for a week in advance. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he asked the question. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had already asked a thousand times. <break time="0.8s" /> Have you ever had a young girl. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Eloise Vashner among your lodgers. <break time="0.8s" /> She is a fair girl of medium height, slender. <break time="0.8s" /> With reddish gold hair. <break time="0.8s" /> And a dark mole near her left eyebrow. <break time="0.8s" /> He explained. <break time="0.8s" /> And she probably sings on the stage. <break time="0.8s" /> The housekeeper did not remember the name. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying that stage people change their names. <break time="0.8s" /> As often as their rooms. <break time="0.8s" /> And that they come and they go. <break time="0.8s" /> For five months he had searched without rest. <break time="0.8s" /> Questioning managers, agents, schools, and choruses. <break time="0.8s" /> And searching theaters. <break time="0.8s" /> From the finest stages down to the lowest music halls. <break time="0.8s" /> He had loved her best. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was sure. <break time="0.8s" /> That she was somewhere in this great city. <break time="0.8s" /> Which, like a monstrous quicksand. <break time="0.8s" /> Kept shifting and swallowing everything without a trace.
